title: 1991 AMC 8 Problem 20
statement:
In the addition problem shown, each digit has been replaced by a letter. If different letters represent different digits, then \(C = \)

\[\begin{array}{cccc} & A & B & C \\ & & A & B \\ + & & & A \\ \hline & 3 & 0 & 0 \end{array}\]

solutions.text:
The three numbers add to \(111A + 11B + C = 300.\) Since \(A = 1\) is too small and \(A \ge 3\) is too large, \(A = 2.\)

Then \(11B + C = 78,\) which forces \(B = 7\) and \(C = 1.\) So \(C = 1.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A .
hints: Write the sum in terms of \(A, B, C\)
